cases.notes: Introduced by Remington in 1963; can be used in its original form or necked into other cases.
Modern case design with .308 Winchester-level ballistic performance in a short-action format.
Durable construction and precision; allows many reloadings.
Designed for a broad range of shooting tasks; intended to drive 220 grain bullets at subsonic velocities and also supports lightweight 125 grain bullets.
Developed from the .338 Norma Magnum necked down to .30 caliber; adopted as the US military’s Advanced Sniper Cartridge for extra-long ranges beyond 1500 meters.
Lapua flagship case; premium consistency and quality; described as the standard for the caliber.
Small rifle primer case developed with the US Palma team; designed to deliver enhanced long-range accuracy.
Also designated .32 S&W Long wadcutter; described as a solid base for pistol-cartridge reloading.
Designed for long-range shooting; case accuracy, reloadability and repeatability are described as unbeaten.
Developed as a long-range sporting cartridge; standardized by CIP in 2010.
Small rifle primer; optimized ignition and better accuracy than large primers in mid-sized cartridges such as the Creedmoor.
Tailored to fit the AR-15 action; designed for light recoil and accuracy.
Match-quality brass that can be loaded more times than brass from competitors.
Base diameter and loading length similar to .308 Winchester; accepts the same bolt heads and fits similar actions and magazines; parent case for several wildcats.
Long popular in Scandinavia; also used by shooters and hunters elsewhere.
New case; necked-down version of the 6.5 Creedmoor; small rifle primer and small flash-hole design; properly annealed at the neck and shoulder; head metallurgy chosen for durability.
Finnish innovation; manufactured by Lapua for almost a century; used in military, Scandinavian hunting and traditional rifle competitions.
Offers a combination of power, light recoil and accuracy; suited to a shorter action.
Popular European hunting caliber; described as a medium-size game hunting round.
Reloading component for double rifles and combination guns; optimized for tens of reloading cycles.
Reloading component for double rifles, drillings and vierlings; optimized for tens of reloading cycles.
Used for big-game hunting in Europe and elsewhere; described as accurate, versatile and powerful.
Designed for big-game hunting; described as a top choice for large and dangerous game.
Also known as 9mm Parabellum or 9x19mm; described as one of the most popular pistol cartridges in the world.

Necked-down version of the 6.5 Creedmoor; able to use a wide range of bullet weights; excellent choice for varmint hunting and long-range shooting; becoming a popular coyote hunting cartridge due to its good knock-down power, light recoil and flat trajectory.

Originating over 100 years ago as a wildcat; became a commercial cartridge in 1969; based off of a necked down 30-06 case; known for superb accuracy and a great balance of power and recoil; suitable as a long-range varmint cartridge and for whitetail and antelope with proper bullet selection.
Based off the 30-06 Springfield; originally designed over 100 years ago; became a factory chambering in the late 80s; with proper bullet selection, well suited for any of North America's big game.
